title: The Theramax study – mild therapeutic hypothermia in hypoxic patients despite maximum VV-ECMO blood flow
summary:
Venovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV ECMO) is an artificial lung that is used in patients with severe respiratory insufficiency, despite optimal ventilation therapy.
Here, the patients are deprived of venous blood with low oxygen, passed through the oxygenator and returned venously as oxygen-rich blood. 
The more blood flows over the membrane per unit of time, the more oxygen is supplied to the body.
Depending on the severity of the pulmonary disease, it may happen that the VV-ECMO must completely replace the lungs of the patients (e.B. in the context of acute respiratory distress syndome (ARDS)). 

To maintain sufficient oxygenation, high blood flows or maximum flow (5-7 l/min) over the membrane are often required. 
The bloodstream of the VV-ECMO is parallel to the cardiovascular system with the functionless lungs:

 
If more blood per time circulates through the functionless lungs (equivalent to cardiac output) than through the VV ECMO, oxygen-depleted blood is pumped through the body. It leads to potentially life-threatening hypoxia with destruction of tissue. 
Since the cardiac output can far exceed the maximum flow of VV ECMO, severe hypoxia can occur in patients despite maximum blood flow at the VV-ECMO. 

An escalation of therapy is not available in this case, as measures to maintain sufficient oxygenation with maximum blood flow via the VV-ECMO have been exhausted. 

We would like to restore the vital adequate oxygenation in these patients through mild therapeutic hypothermia (MTH):

Due to a reduction in cardiac output in MTH, less oxygen-poor blood recirculates from the body's circulation. Proportionally, more oxygenated blood is then promoted by the VV-ECMO into the body circulation from the heart, which could lead to improved oxygenation.

Secondly, MTH reduces the oxygen demand and has a cell-protective effect on hypoxia.

interventions.name:
Intervention: 
Lowering the core body temperature to 34°C

Intervention period:
48h from reaching the target temperature

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Age >18 years 
- Intensive medical therapy with invasive mechanical ventilation of any indication
- VV-ECMO with blood flow > 5l/min
- Persistent hypoxia (pO² < 60mmHg; >6h) with optimal ventilation and VV ECMO therapy
- Deep analgosedation (RASS -5)
Exclusion criteria:
- Severe intra-abdominal, thoracic, gastrointestinal and/or intracerebral bleeding 
- Hemophilia/severe thrombocytopenia (<20)
- Coagulation failure (Quick < 50)
- septic/cardiogenic shock
- Severe circulatory instability
- Pregnancy
